Changelog

boundarylogic 0.2.0

Breaking changes

  • bl_find_local_cf() now applies the thesis’s plausibility rule (section 4.3.1): the counterfactual is selected from a local decision boundary within the convex hull of the training data. For each component pair, the convex hull of the training data and the target is rebuilt on the rotated plane, as in Appendix A of the thesis, and only the boundary points inside it are kept, before the actionability, train_ranges and model filters. The global biplot’s hull polygon is still not used, since the rotation invalidates it. The new argument hull = TRUE is the default; hull = FALSE reproduces the earlier search exactly. The result gains the fields hull and hull_polygon (the winning plane’s hull), and the no-solution message names the hull. Results change where the nearest boundary point lay outside the hull: on the Pima example (Paper 1), 11 of the 79 test targets move, none loses its counterfactual, and the TP target’s constrained runs that hold Age now have none. The loan harness is unchanged. Decided by Adriaan Rowan on 2026-11-05; see documentation/local-convex-hull.md.
  • bl_prepare_data()’s hull_fraction default is now 1 (no outlier removal; it was 0.9), as in the thesis, where outlier removal is optional. Pass hull_fraction = 0.9 to remove the outermost 10% of the training rows, as the thesis’s loan example and the package’s loan harness and vignette do. Code that relied on the old default keeps every training row now. bl_filter_outliers() keeps 0.9, since calling it means filtering is wanted.
  • The distance now follows the thesis rule by projection (thesis section 3.9.1): Euclidean distance for a PCA biplot, Mahalanobis distance for a CVA biplot. The new default distance = "auto" resolves it in bl_find_local_cf() (the pair comparison and the "integer" rounding) and in plot.bl_boundary() / bl_robustness() (the variable-importance standardisation). Under PCA the defaults change: the pairs are compared by Euclidean distance in X-space, and the importance divides by the total standard deviation (X_sd), as in the thesis; pass distance = "mahalanobis" to reproduce earlier PCA results. Under CVA nothing changes. Made on explicit instruction (2026-11-05); it resolves the deferred PCA selector question (rotation note §4.4).
  • bl_find_local_cf(distance = "euclidean") now measures in X-space, each feature divided by its total standard deviation, as bl_find_boundary()’s dist_x (it was the distance on the rotated 2D plane). Under a standardised PCA the two are equal at the search’s point, since the rotated loadings are orthonormal; the X-space distance also measures the "integer" candidates correctly, which lie off the plane. Under CVA an explicit "euclidean" is a different metric from the plane distance, whose ranking equals the Mahalanobis one. bl_find_local_cf() returns the new fields dist_x and all_distances_x, and its print shows them.
  • bl_find_sparse_cf()’s round_to is deprecated: a non-NULL value stops with a message. It rounded in model units (z-scores for a standardised model), one value for every feature, without re-checking the constraints, and could reverse a move and invalidate the sparse counterfactual. Mark a whole-number feature "integer" in set_filters() instead (see below). round_to = NULL still runs.
  • A "fixed" constraint in set_filters() is now strict. When the restored point (the search’s boundary point with each moved fixed feature set back to its observed value) no longer crosses the boundary, or leaves train_ranges, bl_find_local_cf() reports no counterfactual: solution_found is FALSE, fixed_check is kept with applied = FALSE, and blocking_constraint (also given as a message) says where the search moved the fixed feature, why the restored point fails, and that changing the constraints on the actionable features may make a counterfactual possible. Previously the search’s point was kept, so a reported counterfactual could move a “fixed” feature by up to 0.5 model units. A reported counterfactual now always holds every fixed feature exactly. See documentation/fixed-constraint-restore.md.
  • bl_find_local_cf()’s max_pairs default is now 21L (was 10L), so the search tries every eigenvector pair for up to 7 features, as the thesis does. Results change for models with 6 or more features: more pairs are tried, the selected pair can change, and run time grows with the number of pairs. Pass max_pairs = 10L to reproduce earlier results.
  • rotate_deg is removed from plot.bl_local_result() and plot.bl_sparse_result(); passing it stops with an error. rotate_deg is only for viewing the global biplot (plot_biplotEZ(), plot.bl_surrogate() keep it). The local biplot’s orientation is fixed by the optimal rotation (.bl_rotate()), which is part of the method, and is never turned further. This also removes a display bug: with rotate_deg != 0, the sparse-CF cross was drawn in the unrotated frame.
  • rounding parameter replaced by b_margin in bl_build_grid() and bl_build_result(); bl_find_local_cf() reads it from bl_result$b_margin. b_margin sets the decision boundary contour band half-width directly (default 0.001, equivalent to the old rounding = 3L), instead of indirectly via b_margin = 1/10^rounding. Model predictions are unaffected — they are always floor-rounded to 3 d.p.
  • no_points renamed to plot_points in plot_biplotEZ() and plot.bl_local_result(), with positive semantics (TRUE = show points). Defaults preserve prior visual behaviour for each function. (plot.bl_surrogate() has neither argument; it always draws its points.)
  • RForrest model type renamed to RForest in bl_fit_model(), bl_wrap_model(), .fit_model(), and .pred_function(). The old spelling is still accepted at all four entry points but issues a warning and is redirected to RForest.
  • bl_fit_model() now supports only four model types — GLM, SVM, NNET, RForest — all fitted via the parsnip/tidymodels backend. GAM, GBM, LDA, and XGB were removed from bl_fit_model(); use bl_wrap_model() for these (see its predict_fn contract for custom/GAM models, and the mandated list(model = <xgb.Booster>, features = <character vector>) form for XGB).
  • bl_prepare_data() now performs outlier filtering internally via a new hull_fraction parameter (default 0.9) and always returns a "bl_filter_result" object — the previous two-step bl_prepare_data() |> bl_filter_outliers() pattern is collapsed into one call. bl_filter_outliers() remains exported for advanced/iterative use (e.g. after bl_wrap_data()), but is no longer part of the standard workflow.

New features

  • set_filters() accepts an "integer" constraint for a whole-number feature (a count or a score): "integer" alone, with a direction, c("increase", "integer"), or with a range, list(c(min, max), "integer"). Without it a feature is continuous. bl_find_local_cf() searches as before, then rounds the counterfactual: for each integer feature it tries the whole values just below and above, in raw units when a scaling is set, keeps the combinations that still cross the boundary and meet every constraint and train_ranges, and takes the nearest by the search’s selector. When none is valid it reports no counterfactual, with the reason. The Shapley values and the sparse counterfactual use the rounded point. The new field integer_check records the outcome, and print() explains it.
  • bl_find_boundary() gains a dist_mahalanobis field: the squared Mahalanobis distance of each observation’s move to its boundary point, v' W^-1 v with v = B_x - x_obs and W^-1 = bl_result$metric_inv. It is the same quantity as bl_find_local_cf()’s field of that name, so global and local distances can be compared directly. print() shows the mean of its square root. It is NA, with a warning, for a bl_result without metric_inv. No search result changes.
  • New bl_apply_scaling(data, bl_result) converts new data given in raw units, such as an external applicant, to the model’s units with the scaling recorded by bl_set_scaling(). bl_set_scaling() is display-only, so every function that takes new data (bl_select_target(), bl_project_points(), plot(..., target_point =)) expects model units. bl_select_target() now warns when a data-frame target lies outside the training ranges, and suggests bl_apply_scaling() when the target looks like raw units.
  • Added Mahalanobis-aware distance measures, replacing per-feature Euclidean (divided by total SD) with squared Mahalanobis distance using the within-class covariance matrix W:
    • bl_find_local_cf() gains a distance = c("mahalanobis", "euclidean") parameter governing the cross-pair eigenvector-pair selector. New result fields dist_mahalanobis, all_distances_mahalanobis, distance.
    • bl_robustness() and plot.bl_boundary() gain the same distance parameter governing the per-feature standardisation denominator (sqrt(diag(W)) instead of total SD X_sd). plot.bl_boundary() also prints a Mahalanobis check, with a note when the per-feature measure leaves out at least 25% (in absolute value) of the full squared Mahalanobis distance.
    • bl_build_projection() now computes and stores the metric matrix and its Cholesky-based inverse (metric, metric_inv, metric_type), propagated through bl_assemble() into bl_result. See documentation/boundary-distance-and-robustness.md for the full derivation.
    • Both new measures default to "mahalanobis"; pass distance = "euclidean" to reproduce the legacy behaviour exactly. Older bl_result objects without metric_inv fall back to Euclidean with a warning.
  • Added a unified plot() interface for every biplot-producing object — bl_result, bl_local_result, bl_sparse_result, bl_surrogate — via a new plot.bl_result() S3 method and shared private helpers .make_label_line_vec() and .apply_biplot_rotation().
  • Added ticks_var/ticks_n parameters to plot_biplotEZ(), plot.bl_local_result(), and plot.bl_surrogate() for per-variable axis tick-mark count overrides (mirrors the existing label_offset_var/label_offset_dist pattern).
  • plot_biplotEZ() gains rotate_deg (visual rotation), label_cex, and a label_dir = "Paral" default (border-adaptive label direction, replacing "Hor"); label_offset_var now accepts character variable names as well as integer indices.
  • bl_find_boundary()’s out-of-range message reworded to clarify that identified counterfactuals outside the training feature ranges are retained, not discarded.
  • bl_find_local_cf() now restores "fixed" features after the search. The search still lets a fixed feature move by up to 0.5 model units, because a point on the 2D boundary rarely holds a feature at exactly its observed value. Each fixed feature the search moved is then set back to its observed value; if that point still crosses the boundary (and lies within train_ranges), it becomes the counterfactual. A new fixed_check field records the outcome and the search’s own point. Results without a moved fixed feature are unchanged. See documentation/fixed-constraint-restore.md.
  • print() of a bl_local_result now ends with an observed / counterfactual / change / constraint table (raw units when a scaling is set), plus a note explaining any "fixed" feature the search moved. print() of a bl_sparse_result uses the same table layout, with sparse and used columns.
  • bl_shapley() adds a "No effect" class for a Shapley value of 0 (the feature’s change never moves the prediction). For a class-0 target such a feature was previously labelled "Supports" and changed in the sparse counterfactual; for a class-1 target it was labelled "Contradicts". print() of a bl_shapley uses the same comparison-table layout, with shapley and contribute columns and the Shapley sum.
  • bl_find_sparse_cf() now selects features greedily: it changes the "Supports" features one at a time, largest Shapley value first, re-scores the model after each, and stops once the boundary is crossed. Features not needed stay at their observed values. The new field sparse_path records each step, and print() shows it. Previously every "Supports" feature was changed. See documentation/sparse-counterfactual.md, which also records how round_to was used and the "integer" constraint that replaced it.

Bug fixes and other improvements

  • Every biplot now uses the thesis colours for the four prediction outcomes: TP red, TN blue, FP purple, FN orange. plot.bl_projection() (through bl_build_projection()’s point_col) used green, steel blue, orange and red, so red meant FN there and TP everywhere else. The colours are held in one private constant, .confusion_cols (R/utils.R).
  • bl_find_local_cf() warns when the target lies at the centre of the biplot: the Procrustes cross-product is then zero, the rotation is undefined, and every component pair gives the plane of components (1,2). Results are unchanged.
  • The help pages and messages of bl_find_local_cf() and plot.bl_local_result() say “component pair”, not “eigenvector pair”: each pair labels a plane through the target, which the Procrustes rotation turns, so the selected plane need not coincide with the plane of the two components that name it. The rotate_deg error names the Procrustes rotation.
  • The README’s constraint example finds a counterfactual (it found none) and shows its output; the loan harness’s first biplot is titled “no prior default”, which matches its data.
  • plot.bl_shapley() labels every variable "variable: observed -> counterfactual", with and without a recorded scaling. Without a scaling it showed the observed value and the change (e.g. "Age: 22 -> -0.88"), which read as a negative age. Observed and counterfactual now share the decimals of the comparison tables (2, more where the change would print as 0.00), as do the Shapley values on the bars, which are no longer clipped at the plot’s edge. The x-axis reads “Impact on prediction (Shapley value)”. The display rules are written up in documentation/scaling_axis_relabel_note.md.
  • The observed / counterfactual / change tables of print() for bl_local_result, bl_shapley and bl_sparse_result, the Target and Counterfactual blocks, and the sparse path now print in fixed notation with 2 decimals. They printed with 4 decimals and switched to scientific notation when a column mixed large and small values. A feature whose change would print as 0.00 gets more decimals (up to 4) in its row, so a small move such as a loan-to-income change of -0.0016 stays visible. print.bl_target() and print.bl_counterfactual() gain a digits argument, which print.bl_local_result() uses to keep its blocks consistent.
  • plot.bl_boundary()’s Mahalanobis diagnostic now describes the plotted measure. Its “diagonal” used diag(W^-1), which is not what the plot divides by (sqrt(diag(W))); for correlated features (W^-1)_jj >= 1/W_jj, so the printed “cross-correlation” share mostly measured that mismatch (-42.6% on the loan harness). The renamed “Mahalanobis check” compares the squared length of the plotted distances, sum(vec_to_boundary_sd^2), with the full v' W^-1 v (+17.7% on the same run), and returns the numbers as a new mahalanobis_check field. See documentation/boundary-distance-and-robustness.md §4.2.
  • bl_find_boundary(), bl_surrogate() and bl_find_local_cf() are now deterministic. Their shared helper .nearest_idx_block() picked the nearest contour vertex with max.col(-d2), whose default ties.method = "random" treats every vertex within 1e-5 of the farthest vertex’s squared distance as tied and draws one from the session’s random-number stream. Results could therefore change between repeated calls and depend on what had been called before (and on any set.seed()). It now takes the exact nearest vertex (ties.method = "first"). The behaviour was inherited from the PhD code. In the loan harness, 1-3% of global counterfactuals could change under the old rule. Their 2D distance moved by less than 1e-4, but their feature values moved by up to 0.36 training SDs and their model score by up to 0.18. See documentation/nearest-vertex-tie-break.md.
  • Documentation: the help for bl_find_local_cf() no longer says the "euclidean" selector is “not comparable across pairs”. Under CVA the two distance options are the same criterion: the CVA loadings satisfy V'WV = I/(n-g) for every rotated basis, so the squared Mahalanobis distance is n - g times the squared in-plane distance for every pair, and both pick the same pair. Under PCA they differ, and the thesis’s rule is the Euclidean one. The rotation and pair-selection material is now one note, documentation/biplot-rotation/biplot_rotation_and_pair_selection.md (the original PhD method, the implementation, its problems, a proposed solution, and future work); the Mahalanobis note is renamed documentation/boundary-distance-and-robustness.md and covers Phase 2 only.
  • bl_build_grid() now takes its cutoff from the model by default (cutoff = bl_model$cutoff) and stores it as bl_grid$cutoff; bl_assemble() stops if the grid’s and the model’s cutoffs differ. Previously the grid always drew its contours at 0.5 (bl_build_result() passed no cutoff), while bl_find_boundary(), bl_surrogate() and bl_find_local_cf() used bl_result$cutoff, so a model built with another cutoff gave a global boundary at one threshold and a local one at another, without warning. Results at the default 0.5 are unchanged.
  • The "XGB" model type now accepts models from xgboost::xgboost() (class "xgboost"), which are scored from the data frame because their predict method refuses an xgb.DMatrix. bl_wrap_model() stops unless such a model is a binary:logistic classifier on levels "0"/"1": fitted with a numeric response, xgboost() gives a regression. xgb.train() boosters are scored as before.
  • bl_build_projection() with CVA: if a TP/TN/FP/FN group is empty, a message names it and the empty level is dropped, as is any empty level of a user-supplied cva_classes, so CVA and the metric W count only groups with rows. plot.bl_projection() now uses the confusion colours for any subset of the four groups; with an empty group it previously coloured every point blue.
  • bl_find_sparse_cf(): used_in_sparse is now FALSE for a "fixed" feature, which the sparse counterfactual always reverts. It previously followed the Shapley classification alone and could read TRUE for a feature the sparse counterfactual did not change.
  • bl_prepare_data(), bl_filter_outliers(), bl_build_grid() and bl_build_result() no longer change the active graphics device when more than one device is open. The internal helpers .build_hull_polygon() and .bl_get_plot_bounds() now restore the caller’s device after closing their temporary png().
  • plot.bl_local_result() now colours the target by its own true class. Previously it looked the class up in test_data by row number, which gave another observation’s class whenever bl_select_target() indexed a different data frame. bl_target gains a class_obs field; a one-row data frame target that includes the class column now gets its confusion colour too.
  • label_offset_dist and ticks_n now stay paired with their own variables when label_offset_var or ticks_var names a variable the model does not have. Previously the unknown name was dropped but its value was not, so every later value shifted one variable along. A warning now also flags a value vector whose length is neither 1 nor the length of its variable vector. Affects plot_biplotEZ(), plot.bl_local_result() and plot.bl_surrogate() (display only).
  • plot.bl_boundary() printed 25%% instead of 25% in its cross-correlation note.
  • print.bl_result() and summary.bl_result() now label the stored hull fraction as the grid hull (outlie, default 1) rather than as the outlier filter’s fraction, which bl_prepare_data() applies earlier.
  • DESCRIPTION now lists grDevices, graphics, stats and utils under Imports, matching the NAMESPACE imports.
  • Documentation brought in line with the code across the roxygen help, the README, the vignette prose, the implementation summary and the code walkthroughs (for example: bl_build_result(bl_model = NULL) returns a model-free bl_result; bl_filter_outliers() takes a bl_data from bl_wrap_data(); dist_z / dist_mahalanobis belong to the winning pair only; the sparse-CF cross is green/yellow; XGB models must come from xgboost::xgb.train()).
  • Fixed .bl_rotate(): when the selected eigenvector pair is not (1, 2), the target point no longer collapses to the biplot origin. Vrho/tVrho are now sliced to columns/rows (1, 2) unconditionally, matching the SVD construction guarantee.
  • Removed the unsuppressable zero-length-arrow warning from plot_biplotEZ()’s boundary overlay by moving counterfactual-arrow rendering exclusively into bl_pick_point(bl_result, bl_boundary = ...), where it fires at most once per interactive click rather than once per observation at plot-flush time. The boundary, show_arrows, and arrow_col parameters were removed from plot_biplotEZ() accordingly.
  • Swapped the filter order inside bl_find_local_cf()’s per-pair search: set_filters (actionability) now runs before train_ranges (feasibility), enabling an early per-segment exit on the more selective constraint.
  • Added a condition-number check (kappa(V, exact = FALSE)) before solve(V) in bl_build_projection(), with a new condition_number field on the returned object and a warning above 1e10.
  • Clamped grid prediction probabilities to [0, 1] in bl_build_grid(), with a warning reporting how many cells were clamped.
  • bl_surrogate() now reports hull_coverage, n_in_hull, and n_total, surfaced by print.bl_surrogate() alongside accuracy.
  • bl_shapley() / .shapley_perm_one() default changed from seed = 1L to seed = NULL (only seeds the RNG when explicitly requested), so repeated calls on the permutation path (more than exact_max_vars features) are no longer silently deterministic. The exact path (the default for up to 14 features) is deterministic and ignores seed.
  • Guarded bl_assemble() against a bl_model = NULL crash; replaced two silent invisible(NULL) error paths in bl_build_result() with explicit stop() calls; guarded print.bl_points() against missing model predictions with a "(no model)" fallback; .fit_model() now warns on unknown hyperparameters passed via model_params.
  • Fixed the xgboost::xgboost() → xgboost::xgb.train() API migration (data → x, eta → learning_rate, separate required y) in example scripts after an upstream xgboost release changed the interface.
  • Numerous roxygen2 documentation corrections (e.g. bl_predict() rounding documented as 3 d.p., not 4; bl_surrogate()/bl_build_projection() @return fields synchronised with the objects they describe).

boundarylogic 0.1.0 (2026-03-25)

  • Initial implementation of the full three-phase Boundary Logic workflow:
    • Phase 1 — data preparation (bl_prepare_data(), bl_wrap_data(), bl_filter_outliers()), model fitting/wrapping (bl_fit_model(), bl_wrap_model()), PCA/CVA biplot projection (bl_build_projection()), prediction-grid and decision-boundary contour construction (bl_build_grid()), and assembly into the central bl_result anchor object (bl_assemble(), bl_build_result()), with plot_biplotEZ() for visualisation.
    • Phase 2 (global) — nearest-boundary counterfactual search (bl_find_boundary()), distance-to-boundary plots and per-variable robustness summaries (plot.bl_boundary(), bl_robustness()), and a spatial surrogate model (bl_surrogate()).
    • Phase 3 (local) — single-observation target selection (bl_select_target()), actionability constraints (set_filters()), local counterfactual search via biplot rotation (bl_find_local_cf()), Shapley attribution of the counterfactual path (bl_shapley()), and sparse counterfactual generation (bl_find_sparse_cf()).
  • Interactive biplot point picker bl_pick_point().
  • bl_predict() and bl_project_points() for scoring and projecting arbitrary data frames into the biplot’s Z-space.
  • Bundled the Pima Indians Diabetes and loan-default datasets, with accompanying vignettes covering the complete workflow end to end.
